caption.body:
The part nobody warns you about isn't the editing. It's the scrubbing.

You know the tangent is somewhere near the twenty-minute mark. So you drag, listen, overshoot, drag back. Four minutes to find a cut that takes four seconds to make — and there are eight more like it waiting.

Eight of those nine jobs a transcript pass handles on its own. The ninth one stays yours, and it should: deciding a tangent went nowhere is a judgement about your own episode, and that is the only part of the evening actually worth spending.

Fair warning — it works off the transcript, so a rough recording gives you a rough transcript and you will spend the time reading instead. Audio only: no video, no multitrack, and you still publish it yourself.

Which of the nine eats the most of your evening? Mine was pauses, for years.
